notes: **Statement 005-N1.** The page completes the table with multistrates M, described as the strictly irreducible objects of the figure poset, and lieux L, with a cancelled definition replaced by minimal elements of the nonempty figures for ≪. The upper-left note defines strata, déployement, and incidence X◁F. At 1 asserts nonemptiness and existence of bounded suprema; At 2 expresses each figure as the supremum of its strata (Grothendieck, 1986, scan 5). These definitions and axioms are recorded as background.

**Statement 005-N2.** The Scholie describes a family of lower closed subsets of M, lists a–c and the alternative primed conditions, and later defines compatibility through existence of a join. The foot states a reconstruction claim for figures of t.f. using At 1–3 and gives reflexivity/symmetry wording plus downward compatibility. The full representation and reconstruction claims were not independently proved in this run.

**Statement 005-N3 — targeted check.** For figures F and G, At 2 gives the displayed inclusion criterion: if F≤G, choose Y=X for each stratum X of F; conversely, X≤Y≤G for every such X makes G an upper bound of F’s strata, hence F≤G. This proof concerns the displayed F/G equivalence and does not resolve the preceding C|G glyph. The same narrow argument was independently recorded by R2.

**Statement 005-N4 — targeted check.** Condition b makes family nonemptiness equivalent to membership of the empty subset, since the empty subset is closed in any member. If the union in c is read as the union of all family members, that family is automatically nonempty for nonempty M. This second implication is conditional on the membership-index interpretation; it does not resolve the plus-like index in the ink. R2 independently recorded these two short implications. Detailed scope and steps are retained in records/scan005_math_checks.md.

**Reading decisions prompted by mathematics.** The mapping-looking mark is drawn as a horizontal shaft with two transverse end strokes, without introducing a pointed arrowhead. The next set letter is visibly F(M), despite the natural powerset expectation. The b′ set carries a straight overbar, unlike the neighbouring tilde; it is not silently changed. The index of the union remains +|∈. The compatibility definition retains F∨C. Its displayed bounded pair is read {F,G} from the inward return of G, after reviewing R3’s C|G doubt. The final first condition has X, a compatibility sign, then réflexive symétrique, without a second X.

**Recovered state and literal irregularities.** The underline beneath the cancelled éléments is placed with that original baseline; lieux is inserted above. The nonemptiness pointer and the bent connector beneath the inserted axiom names are drawn. The latter has no parentheses: the apparent opening curve descends from the f of figures above. A crop of an agreed word led all three readers, in separately preserved supplementary readings, to favour parties in “comme une parties”; the final text marks parties|partie. Fermés, déployement, unpointed ens, the lower-case x occurrences, and the tentative toutes before singular famille are kept literally.

**Qualifications and dating.** “Dans le cas où les figures sont de t.f.” conditions the reconstruction claim. No explicit proof-check request or new date/title is present. The manuscript page number is 4 over a doubtful earlier 3. Erased axiom labels and overwritten starts remain marked rather than reconstructed from the numbering.
